purpose: Resolve the policy-to-product, enforcement-workflow, deployment, consequence, contestability, oversight, and ideological-implementation fog in the bounded ICE immigration-enforcement lane. The wave distinguishes documented policy alignment and system design from unproved case-level causation, weak contestability, unlawfulness, or system-wide ideological governance.

method.null_hypothesis: a lawful executive enforcement policy implemented through ordinary agency contracting, human decision processes, and multiple information systems
method.promotion_rule: An official policy, contract requirement, award, or oversight record may establish the doctrine, system-design, deployment, workflow, funding, or counterpower transition it expressly names. A designed enforcement workflow does not establish a particular person's consequence, error, lack of discretion, failed appeal, or unlawful implementation.
method.source_rule: Official White House, USAspending, congressional, and agency records are treated as source-bounded. Public text mirrors of SAM.gov attachments remain secondary custody pending preservation of the primary attachment bytes.

records.proposition: ICE's ImmigrationOS requirements operationalize bounded elements of Executive Order 14159's enforcement, identification, prioritization, voluntary-departure, detention, and removal policy.

sources.title: Executive Order 14159: Protecting the American People Against Invasion

records.observation: Executive Order 14159 directs total and efficient immigration-law enforcement, prioritization of specified noncitizens, enhanced identification and information sharing, detention, voluntary departure, and efficient or expedited removal. The recovered ImmigrationOS requirement text describes targeting and enforcement prioritization, self-deportation tracking, and immigration-lifecycle management from identification through removal.
supports: an R6 doctrine-to-product-design transition in one bounded ICE lane
connection between an official enforcement policy and named software requirements
a dated policy, procurement, and workflow-design chronology
does_not_support: that every ImmigrationOS feature derives exclusively from the executive order
weak contestability, failed appeal, or absence of human discretion
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Preserve the official ImmigrationOS statement of work, requirements, product backlog, change requests, acceptance criteria, architecture, user stories, legal review, privacy review, civil-rights assessment, and policy-to-feature traceability matrix.
records.falsifier: The operative requirements materially predate or do not implement the cited policy elements, or the named functions were not delivered, accepted, or used.

records.proposition: ImmigrationOS became a deployed operational capability supporting ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations rather than remaining an unimplemented prototype concept.

sources.title: ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations modernization and operational capability award

records.observation: The continuation record describes ImmigrationOS as an existing system deployed for Enforcement and Removal Operations. The May 2026 USAspending record identifies a Palantir award for ERO modernization and operational capability for the enforcement case-management system on the case-management and analytics platform, with approximately $86.27 million shown as the award obligation and outlay in the retrieved record snapshot.
supports: I3 operating-layer review in a bounded ERO modernization lane
continued public funding and operational support after prototype development
a named agency component, platform, mission, period, and financial instrument
does_not_support: that ImmigrationOS is the only ERO operating system
a specific apprehension, detention, voluntary departure, or removal
the accuracy of every secondary attachment-text field
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire official attachment bytes, the prototype-to-production transition decision, complete task order, option and modification history, production acceptance, active-user and workflow evidence, uptime, defects, performance, alternatives, transition plan, and actual obligation/outlay reconciliation.
records.falsifier: The system was not deployed operationally, was not used by ERO, or remained an optional or marginal overlay with practical alternatives and no material workflow role.

records.proposition: The ImmigrationOS procurement describes a designed workflow from identity and case information through targeting, prioritization, voluntary-departure tracking, and removal operations.
records.observation: The recovered procurement text identifies three principal capability areas: targeting and enforcement prioritization, self-deportation tracking, and immigration-lifecycle management from identification through removal. Those requirements describe a designed enforcement chain, not a completed case-level consequence record.
supports: a bounded H3 workflow-design chain
the intended conversion of identity and case information into enforcement prioritization and removal support
a concrete acquisition target for decision rules, data, discretion, consequence, and correction review
does_not_support: which data sources or classifications were actually used
whether a model, rule, officer, or supervisor made a particular decision
a completed removal, detention, arrest, or departure
error rate, correction, appeal, or contestability
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the data dictionary, source inventory, identity joins, targeting and priority rules, user interface, role permissions, human approvals, audit logs, exception handling, case chronology, actual consequences, corrections, complaints, appeals, and quality controls.
records.falsifier: The delivered system did not contain or support the described functions, or they were not used in any operational enforcement workflow.

records.proposition: An executive enforcement doctrine was connected to an installed information system designed to support identification, prioritization, tracking, detention or removal operations.

sources.title: Executive Order 14159: Protecting the American People Against Invasion
ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations modernization and operational capability award

records.observation: The bounded record now connects an official enforcement doctrine to named software requirements and later operational funding for ERO case-management and analytics capabilities. It does not yet establish the I4 elements of encoded doctrine at rule level, mandatory or practically inescapable use, weak override or appeal, or a case-level consequence with intent connected to implementation.
supports: policy-to-system-design and deployment review
a narrower ideological-implementation acquisition lane
does_not_support: Palantir causation of every ERO action
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire policy-to-feature traceability, encoded categories and rules, mandatory-use directives, discretion and override records, consequence-specific case traces, notice, correction, administrative and judicial review, alternatives, and intent evidence tied to implementation.
records.falsifier: The system implements neutral case-administration functions independent of the cited doctrine, preserves broad discretion and effective review, and does not materially shape consequential decisions.

records.proposition: The existing record connects a specific person's ImmigrationOS data and priority state to a completed apprehension, detention, voluntary departure, removal, or other material consequence.
records.observation: The policy, procurement, deployment, and funding records describe intended and operational capabilities but contain no source-bounded person-level case chronology joining system input, identity resolution, priority or recommendation, human decision, executed consequence, error, correction, appeal, and final disposition.
supports: an exact case-file acquisition contract
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire lawfully available deidentified case traces, administrative records, declarations, audit samples, litigation records, notices, officer and supervisor decisions, system logs, corrections, appeals, outcomes, and explicit non-links where the system did not materially contribute.
records.falsifier: Complete case samples show ImmigrationOS neither supplied material data nor shaped the prioritization, decision, or consequence.

records.proposition: ICE made a material 2026 public expenditure for Palantir-supported ERO case-management and analytics modernization.

sources.title: ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations modernization and operational capability award

records.observation: The retrieved USAspending record identifies Palantir as recipient of an ICE award beginning May 5, 2026 for ERO modernization and operational capability for an enforcement case-management system on a case-management and analytics platform, with approximately $86.27 million displayed in obligations and outlays in the retrieved snapshot.
supports: a material public-resource-to-vendor award flow
continued investment in the bounded ERO operating lane
an award-level acquisition anchor for performance and residual-rights review
does_not_support: the number or outcome of enforcement actions
award causation by lobbying, litigation, or policy influence
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the signed order, funding and payment ledger, invoices, deliverables, acceptance, performance, costs, options, modifications, refunds, recovery, vendor rights, subcontractors, competition records, and recognized revenue.
records.falsifier: The award data are corrected materially, the work is not Palantir-supported ERO modernization, or funds were not actually obligated, paid, or associated with delivered capability.

records.proposition: Congressional oversight has demanded system, contractor, data-source, legal-authority, safeguard, and operational-use disclosures for ImmigrationOS and related DHS immigration-enforcement tools.

sources.title: Goldman, Wyden, Velázquez Demand Answers on DHS Use of Palantir and Immigration Data Systems

records.observation: Members of Congress requested that DHS identify databases and tools, contractors, data sources, legal authorities, safeguards, sharing practices, accuracy controls, and operational uses associated with Palantir and immigration-enforcement data systems.
supports: an active H4 inspection and accountability intervention
a source-addressed demand for the records needed to complete the consequence and visibility ledgers
evidence that the system's operation and safeguards are contested and subject to oversight
does_not_support: the truth of every concern expressed by the lawmakers
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the oversight letter, DHS and ICE responses, briefings, document productions, inspector and privacy reviews, corrective actions, noncompliance, and later legislative or judicial outcomes.
records.falsifier: The request did not concern the described systems or produced records showing the concerns were factually mistaken and safeguards fully effective.

records.proposition: A flawed federal data-transfer process created a documented risk of misidentified taxpayer information being disclosed to ICE.

sources.title: IRS acknowledges flawed transfer system may have improperly shared taxpayer data with ICE

records.observation: The cited congressional record reports that the IRS acknowledged a flawed transfer process that may have misidentified taxpayers and improperly shared data with ICE. The bounded source does not identify Palantir or ImmigrationOS as the transfer mechanism or receiving decision system.
supports: a real adjacent H4 data-quality and correction risk
the need for source-to-target field lineage and identity validation in immigration-enforcement data systems
a comparator for how documented data error should be preserved
does_not_support: use of the transferred data in targeting or removal
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the IRS and ICE transfer specification, data fields, identity-matching logic, receiving system, audit logs, affected records, correction, notice, downstream use, and explicit Palantir or ImmigrationOS non-link or interface evidence.
records.falsifier: Operative records identify Palantir or ImmigrationOS as a material transfer, matching, or downstream decision component.

records.proposition: The bounded EO 14159 and ImmigrationOS records establish one coordinated founder-controlled system of coercive ideological governance across the full estate.
records.observation: Wave 05 establishes a bounded doctrine-to-system-design relationship, operational ERO funding, a designed enforcement workflow, legislative oversight, and an adjacent federal data-quality failure. It does not establish case-level consequences, weak contestability, a complete Palantir-to-RCA or ImmigrationOS-to-consequence chain, common governance across companies and capital, or system-wide ideological implementation.
supports: continued bounded I4 testing in the ImmigrationOS and ERO lanes
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Require encoded rules, mandatory-use records, consequential case traces, discretion, notice, correction, appeal, alternatives, common governance, cross-system interfaces, and causal private-benefit records across additional lanes.
records.falsifier: Complete system and case records show ordinary case administration, independent human decisions, effective review, no material policy-to-feature encoding, and no common private design across the estate.
